description: Role-scoped craft procedures for Huddle Robos. Seeded entries are installed on first run; the rest can be discovered and adopted during work.
adoption: Search with search_skill_catalog, read the matching entry with read_skill_catalog, then adopt it by id with adopt_skill.

entries.name: Decision Frame
entries.summary: Turn a messy request into a decision, a reason and a next move.
entries.trigger: When a request has several possible directions and no clear decision yet.
entries.invocation: Follow these steps during planning; adopt first if this is not already on your shelf.
steps: Name the decision that has to be made and the constraint that matters most.
List two viable moves and the trade-off that separates them.
Recommend one move, name the first concrete action and the check that proves it worked.
entries.rationale: It keeps strategic work pointed at a decision instead of a survey of options.

entries.name: Pre-Mortem
entries.summary: Find the failure modes in a plan before it becomes a commitment.
entries.trigger: Before committing to a risky plan, launch, migration or multi-step build.
entries.invocation: Use before execution; adopt this entry when the task needs a risk pass.
steps: Assume the plan failed after two weeks and name the three most likely causes.
Separate preventable causes from accepted risks.
Add one guardrail and one stop condition before execution starts.
entries.rationale: A pre-mortem turns optimism into explicit failure handling while there is still time to change the plan.

entries.name: Failing Test Triage
entries.summary: Find the first broken assumption behind a failing test.
entries.trigger: When a test fails and the cause is not yet isolated.
entries.invocation: Follow these steps during debugging; adopt first if this is not already on your shelf.
steps: Read the failure and the smallest code path it exercises.
Reproduce it with one targeted command or test run.
State the broken assumption, fix the narrowest cause, and rerun that test before widening the change.
entries.rationale: It keeps debugging narrow enough to learn the cause instead of masking it with broad edits.

entries.name: Migration Safety Pass
entries.summary: Review a schema or data migration for lock, rollback and deploy-order risk.
entries.trigger: Before changing a schema, running a migration, or reviewing a migration plan.
entries.invocation: Adopt this entry, then apply every step to the migration under review.
steps: State the schema change, row count, lock risk and rollback path before touching the database.
Check for a backward-compatible expand/contract sequence; never make a destructive change in one deploy.
Verify the migration against a staging copy with production-shaped row counts and a timed rollback.
Name the exact success checks and the abort threshold before execution.
entries.rationale: A migration review catches lock and rollback failures before they reach live traffic.

entries.name: Assumption Audit
entries.summary: Expose the unstated premises a plan is resting on.
entries.trigger: When a plan sounds coherent but rests on unstated premises.
entries.invocation: Follow these steps during review; adopt first if this is not already on your shelf.
steps: Write the three assumptions the plan cannot survive without.
Mark each as tested, untested or contradicted, with the evidence.
Name the cheapest test for the most dangerous untested assumption.
entries.rationale: It moves criticism from taste to evidence and gives the Operator a testable next step.

entries.name: Adversarial Review
entries.summary: Stress a proposal the way production will.
entries.trigger: When a proposal is about to ship and needs a hostile read.
entries.invocation: Adopt this entry before the review, then apply it to the actual proposal.
steps: State the strongest case for why the proposal fails in production.
Find the failure mode the author is least likely to have measured.
Give one concrete change that removes or exposes that failure mode.
entries.rationale: An adversarial pass finds the failure the happy-path review missed.

entries.name: Source Reliability Check
entries.summary: Separate primary evidence from summaries and unsupported claims.
entries.trigger: When a conclusion depends on sources whose quality is not yet clear.
entries.invocation: Follow these steps while gathering evidence; adopt first if this is not already on your shelf.
steps: Separate primary evidence from summaries and commentary.
Check who produced each claim and when it was last updated.
Label each key claim as verified, inferred or unresolved.
entries.rationale: It prevents confident synthesis from hiding weak or stale evidence.

entries.name: Evidence Synthesis
entries.summary: Turn scattered sources into a decision-ready answer with the weakest link named.
entries.trigger: When several sources must be reconciled before a decision.
entries.invocation: Adopt this entry when the task needs synthesis, then follow the steps.
steps: Group the evidence by the claim it supports, not by source.
State where sources agree, where they conflict and what is still unknown.
Give the decision-ready conclusion with the weakest link called out.
entries.rationale: It makes the uncertainty explicit instead of averaging conflicting sources into false confidence.

entries.name: Command Preflight
entries.summary: Check a state-changing command before it runs.
entries.trigger: Before running a shell command that changes state.
entries.invocation: Follow these steps before execution; adopt first if this is not already on your shelf.
steps: State the exact command, working directory and expected effect.
Confirm the command is reversible and capture the current state.
Run the narrowest version, inspect the result, then widen only if it is clean.
entries.rationale: A short preflight catches the most expensive operator mistakes before they happen.

entries.name: Incident Timeline
entries.summary: Reconstruct an operational failure as a causal timeline.
entries.trigger: During or immediately after an operational failure.
entries.invocation: Adopt this entry for the incident review, then apply the steps to the evidence.
steps: Record the first observed symptom and the last known good state.
Order events by timestamp and mark the action that changed the system.
End with the smallest prevention and the check that proves it.
entries.rationale: A causal timeline separates the trigger from the damage and points to one preventive change.

entries.name: Durable Summary
entries.summary: Preserve decisions, evidence and open questions so later work can continue.
entries.trigger: When a room has produced decisions, constraints and open questions that must survive.
entries.invocation: Follow these steps when closing a work session; adopt first if this is not already on your shelf.
steps: Keep the decisions, constraints, evidence and open questions separate.
Attribute every claim to its speaker or source.
Write the next action with an owner and a verification point.
entries.rationale: A durable summary lets the next turn resume from evidence instead of re-litigating the room.

entries.name: Decision Log
entries.summary: Record a decision and the condition that would reopen it.
entries.trigger: When a decision will affect later work or another Robo.
entries.invocation: Adopt this entry when maintaining the record, then follow the steps.
steps: Record the decision, date, decision-maker and the problem it resolves.
List the alternatives rejected and the reason.
Name the condition that would reopen the decision.
entries.rationale: A decision log preserves intent, not just the outcome, so future work does not silently reverse it.
